Police Seize Drugs Worth R2.8 Million in Two Busts at OR Tambo Airport, Including Crystal Meth Destined for Philippines and Dagga From Morocco

Police at OR Tambo International Airport seized drugs with a combined street value of R2.8 million during separate operations this week. The busts involved crystal meth and dagga discovered at cargo warehouses, highlighting ongoing law enforcement efforts to intercept illicit substances entering and leaving South Africa.

The first seizure occurred on Wednesday, 4 March 2026, when police discovered crystal meth worth R2.2 million at a cargo warehouse. The meth was reportedly destined for the Philippines. Authorities secured the substances and began an investigation to trace those responsible for attempting to traffic the drugs internationally.

A second seizure took place on Thursday, 5 March 2026, at another cargo warehouse where eight large boxes containing dagga valued at R672 000 were found. The dagga had been shipped from Morocco and was intended for distribution in South Africa. Police secured the shipment and are investigating the source and recipients.

Both drug consignments remain in police custody as investigations continue. Authorities are working to identify and apprehend the traffickers involved. No arrests have been reported at this stage, but the seizures demonstrate continued vigilance by law enforcement at OR Tambo International Airport against drug smuggling and cross-border trafficking.

Some 2,000 families displaced by a fire that struck a residential area in Barangay Pinyahan, Quezon City received aid from the local government, Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) and Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) on Sunday in line with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.'s instruction to provide immediate relief. 

The PCSO said 2,000 “charitimba” (charity pail) containing food and other essential supplies, and modular tents were distributed at the city hall grounds, supervised by Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte, PCSO General Manager Melquiades Robles and MMDA General Manager Nicolas Torre III. https://t.co/W8eGSVXxiM
